description: A two-panel bright-field TEM (BF-TEM) figure comparing the solution-treated microstructures of two Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steels; both panels carry a white "1 µm" scale bar at the lower left and white panel letters (a) and (b). (a) M1-SS: a featureless, uniformly bright austenite matrix traversed only by dark, straight-to-curved boundary lines that meet at a triple junction in the upper-middle of the frame; no second-phase particles are visible. (b) M2-SS: the same bright matrix appearance, but now speckled with numerous fine dark dot-like particles dispersed within the grain interior, together with a curved dark band cutting across the grain and a few larger dark spots; two blue arrows point at the particles and blue text annotates them "(Ti, V) c". Both micrographs use the same 1 µm scale, so the precipitate-free matrix of (a) and the precipitate-decorated matrix of (b) are directly comparable. The figure demonstrates that Ti and V addition produces intragranular precipitates that survive solution treatment, whereas the Ti/V-free M1 matrix remains precipitate-free. No numeric values are printed in either panel.

subfigures.description: Bright-field TEM micrograph of M1-SS with a 1 µm scale bar; a clean, uniformly bright austenite matrix subdivided only by dark straight/curved boundary lines meeting at a triple junction. No precipitates are visible in the grain interior.

Bright-field TEM micrograph of M2-SS with a 1 µm scale bar; the matrix contains numerous fine dark dot-like precipitates dispersed within the grain, a curved dark band, and a few larger dark spots. Two blue arrows point to the particles and blue text labels them '(Ti, V) c'.

observations.observation: Both panels are bright-field TEM micrographs of the same magnification class, each with a 1 µm scale bar in the lower-left corner.
Panel (a) (M1-SS) shows a precipitate-free, uniformly bright austenite matrix whose only contrast features are dark straight-to-curved boundary lines meeting at a triple junction.
Panel (b) (M2-SS) shows fine dark dot-like precipitates dispersed inside the grain interior, indicated by two blue arrows and the blue annotation '(Ti, V) c'.
Panel (b) additionally contains a curved dark band running across the grain and a few larger dark spots not seen in panel (a).
No numeric values (sizes, counts, compositions) are printed inside either micrograph; only the 1 µm scale bars and the panel letters (a)/(b).
The caption states the figure shows BF (bright-field) images of M1-SS (a) and M2-SS (b).

The citing text states that Fig. 3(a) presents the austenite matrix of M1 after solution treatment and that no precipitates are observed because Cr and Mo do not precipitate at the solution temperature.
The citing text states that Fig. 3(b) shows M2-SS microstructure containing precipitates in addition to the matrix.
The citing text identifies the precipitates as (Ti, V)C carbides on the grounds that the precipitation temperatures of Ti and V exceed 1000 °C.
The citing text reports an average intragranular (Ti, V)C carbide size of 35.8 ± 20.1 nm, a value that is not printed in the micrographs and cannot be measured at the supplied resolution.
